clue.text: Could be Woody Allen on vacation on small island

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: Herm is one of the smaller Channel Islands

indicators.note: a word on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its middle, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Woody Allen is pictured holidaying on a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants Woody Allen himself, but 'Woody' belongs to the definition: Woody Herman was an American jazz clarinettist and bandleader. 'on vacation' empties ALLEN to AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by surname: the jazz bandleader Woody Herman, so Woody could be followed by this name.

clue.text: Magician could make a tenner entertaining children

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold or receive, so one set of letters goes inside the other
letters that could make something else are open to rearrangement into a new word

explanation.surface: A conjuror earning ten pounds for amusing a children's party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' turns A TENNER into ENANTER, and 'entertaining' puts CH inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who casts spells or works magic, as in fairy tales.

clue.text: Church wants university for one Irish province

indicators.note: one thing put for another stands in its place, so a letter is swapped out

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A church seeking a university to serve a part of Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' signals the swap: U replaces the I of MINSTER, with 'wants' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: the southern of Ireland's four historic provinces, containing Cork and Kerry.

clue.text: Fix up a drink

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: to pin something is to fix it in place

explanation.surface: Someone asked to make a quick drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns PIN round in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a nip is a small measure of spirits, a dram.

clue.text: One person's close friend? That's about it, on reflection

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so one piece is wrapped round the other

parts.note: an inmate is one person housed in an institution, so the opening words give that resident

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the word it is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before it is turned round

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they have a close friend and admits that is all, after some thought.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits in the middle of the clue; the prisoner of the opening words wraps round the reversed 'it', and 'That's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: someone you are very close to, a confidant.

clue.text: Paper has no time to publish

indicators.note: a word that has no letter is left without it, so that letter is removed

parts.note: tissue is a thin soft paper

explanation.surface: A newspaper too short of time to go to press.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a newspaper, but 'Paper' is tissue paper, which loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to issue a book or statement is to publish or release it.

clue.text: Sports venue deterring canned drinks consumption

indicators.note: a thing that drinks something takes it inside
canned is slang for drunk, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: TB, tuberculosis, was formerly called consumption

explanation.surface: A stadium putting off fans from drinking from cans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canned' is slang for drunk, so it scrambles 'deterring'; 'consumption' is the old name for tuberculosis. Trent Bridge is a Test cricket ground in Nottingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: a famous cricket ground in Nottingham where England play Test matches.

clue.text: Cautiously head off after married Northern woman

indicators.note: the piece that comes after married is placed behind it
with its head off, a word loses its first letter

parts.note: warily means cautiously

explanation.surface: A northern wife taking care to slip away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' cuts the first letter from WARILY, leaving ARILY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a woman's first name, as borne by the film star Marilyn Monroe.

clue.text: Young child's given a large sum

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the standard abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A toddler handed a big sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a total is the sum of figures added together.

clue.text: Sleeps after school, having imbibed Penny's strong drink

indicators.note: the sleeping piece comes after school, so it is placed second
to imbibe is to drink in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: naps are short sleeps
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money

explanation.surface: A pupil napping after lessons, having had a drink from Penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny' looks like a woman's name but is the coin abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a strong colourless spirit, often flavoured, drunk in northern Europe.

clue.text: Mistakes are coming back to bite singer

indicators.note: biting means closing the jaws around something, so one piece goes inside the other
something coming back runs the other way, so the word are is read backwards

parts.note: in slang a singer is an informer, as is a rat

explanation.surface: Blunders return to plague a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'singer' is a criminal who sings to the police, an informer, so the musical picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a list of printed errors, the Latin plural for mistakes.

clue.text: British PM mostly intended axing core defence

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister from 1945 to 1951

indicators.note: axing the core of a word removes its central letter

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A British premier planning to cut a central plank of national defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims ATTLEE to ATTLE, and 'axing core' removes the middle A of MEANT to leave MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in castle terms: a parapet with gaps for shooting, built to defend a wall.

clue.text: He maybe captures new bird? That's right

indicators.note: to capture is to enclose, so these pieces go inside the other

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol for helium, an example of a chemical element
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A man perhaps catching a fresh bird and calling it his due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man, but it is the symbol for helium; 'maybe' marks it as an example. 'captures' puts N and TIT inside ELEMENT, after its first E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an entitlement is a right or claim to something.

clue.text: Supply missing article for plant

indicators.note: a word missing something has those letters removed

parts.note: read as supple plus -ly, supply means in a supple way, which is lithely
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: An order to provide goods, with one item absent, for a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb to provide, but it is the adverb from supple, a meaning of 'lithely'; take out THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a flowering bulb plant with trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Clink glasses tiresomely? Not entirely

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters from inside them

explanation.surface: Someone toasting by tapping glasses rather too often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clink' looks like the noise of glasses, but it is slang for prison; the letters run from the end of 'glasses' into 'tiresomely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: both words mean a prison or jail.

clue.text: Fashion in dress at start of Wimbledon showing glitz

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reworked
the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Clothing styles at the opening of the Wimbledon tennis championships showing off their sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fashion' looks like a noun about clothes but is the verb that shuffles IN DRESS AT with W, the first letter of Wimbledon, a London tennis tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Near synonym: glitz is showy, cheap glamour, and the answer is that cheap, flashy quality.

clue.text: Earned money in Korea

definitions.meaning: past tense of to win, as in prizes earned or gained
the currency unit of both North and South Korea

explanation.surface: Someone earning cash in Korea.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a past form of the verb meaning gained, and the name of the Korean currency.

clue.text: Seething about officer getting whipping

indicators.note: here about means placed around, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: surging means swelling or seething like a sea
CO is the abbreviation for commanding officer

explanation.surface: An angry commanding officer ordering a flogging.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: scourging is flogging with a scourge, a type of whip.

clue.text: Just being locked in bog gets journalist alarmed

indicators.note: something locked in something else is shut up inside it

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, a bog
just means fair or right
ED is the abbreviation for editor, a stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter shut in the lavatory panics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bog' wants to be the toilet, as British slang, but here it is marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: frightened means scared, made afraid.

clue.text: Doctor pockets money, meeting a relative

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: A doctor taking cash while visiting a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a grandfather is a kind of family relative.

clue.text: Spinner's back, finding turn

indicators.note: going back means reading the letters the other way

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy, and the 's adds S

explanation.surface: A cricket spin bowler's back finding some turn off the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinner' suggests a spin bowler in cricket, but it is a spinning top; 'back' turns TOPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a performer's spot is their turn or slot in a show.

clue.text: At sea, it cooks stuff

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rework, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A ship's cook preparing food while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' could itself signal an anagram, but 'cooks' does that job and 'At sea' joins IT as the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to satiate is to fill to excess, to stuff with food.

clue.text: Grand tableau regularly used for celebration

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: at regular intervals, picking every second letter

explanation.surface: A grand scene staged for a festive occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of 'tableau'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gala is a festive celebration or special occasion.

clue.text: Saw notice on time

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a timetable notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of to see, but it is the noun for an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a saw is an old saying, a proverb.

clue.text: Having uncovered mild puncturing, changing a tyre is simple

indicators.note: a piece puncturing another pierces it and sits inside
changing letters puts them in another order
with its covering stripped off a word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: clement means mild, of weather

explanation.surface: Changing a punctured tyre is easy once the mild damage is exposed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges A TYRE to ETARY, and the stripped synonym for 'mild' goes after its first letter. 'Having' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: elementary means basic or straightforward.

clue.text: Indeed, nameless drunk could be Murphy

indicators.note: drunk letters are reeling about, so they are rearranged
without the name, so the abbreviation N for name is removed

explanation.surface: An anonymous drunk might be someone called Murphy, indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N from INDEED, and 'drunk' rearranges IDEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Example by first name: the American comedian and actor Eddie Murphy.

clue.text: Unhappy daughter has extremely large burden

parts.note: sad means unhappy

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its outside letters

explanation.surface: A miserable daughter carrying a huge load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives L and E, the end letters of 'large'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to saddle someone with a task is to burden them.

clue.text: Drive Nancy's friend around at 100? That's impressive

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for drive in addresses

indicators.note: one piece goes around the other

parts.note: Nancy is a French city, and ami is French for friend
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: Someone driving a friend called Nancy at 100 miles per hour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nancy' looks like a woman but is the French city, so the friend is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dramatic means striking or spectacular.

clue.text: American bum's a fool

definitions.meaning: in American English the buttocks are this word, British arse
a donkey, figuratively a stupid person

explanation.surface: An American tramp is an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the American spelling of the slang for backside, and a stupid person.

clue.text: Riposte requires right sword fencing skill

indicators.note: fencing something encloses it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the epee is a fencing sword
art means skill

explanation.surface: A fencer's counter-thrust needs the right sword and skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riposte' and 'fencing' both suggest swordplay, but the riposte is a witty reply and 'fencing' only signals enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: repartee is quick witty retort, a stream of ripostes.

clue.text: Small shelf for hammer

parts.note: a ledge is a narrow shelf

explanation.surface: A little shelf to hold a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a sledge is a large heavy hammer, short for sledgehammer.
